title: Service Path
description: Per-hop request path health (DNS, Cloudflare, rproxy-0/1/2, backend host, application) for homelab services. Answers: where does the request path stop working?

panels.title: Service
panels.description: Virtual host probed for the selected $service.

panels.title: Overall status
panels.description: HEALTHY / DEGRADED / DOWN, derived from service_path:probable_failure_code. UNKNOWN = no probe data.

panels.title: External path
panels.description: Worst hop on Public DNS -> Cloudflare -> rproxy-0 -> back proxies -> host -> app.

panels.title: Internal path
panels.description: Worst hop on Internal DNS -> rproxy-0 -> back proxies -> host -> app.

panels.title: HTTP status (via back proxy)
panels.description: Status code returned when the application health path is requested through the primary back proxy with the service's Host header. 502/504 = proxy is up but cannot reach the backend.

panels.title: Response time (via Cloudflare)
panels.description: Full external round trip: DNS-independent request to the Cloudflare edge, Cloudflare -> origin -> rproxy-0 (stops at the oauth2 sign-in for authenticated sites).

panels.title: Service path: $service
panels.description: Each box is coloured by its own probe (green OK, yellow degraded/slow, red failed, grey no data). Each thick line is the state of that hop; grey means the hop could not be tested (an earlier hop failed or there is no data). Moving dashes appear only on hops that should currently carry traffic: rproxy-2 is an nginx `backup` upstream and only carries traffic when rproxy-1 is down.

options.content:
**How the probable failure location is chosen** (first match wins; from `service_path:probable_failure_code`):

| # | Condition | Shown as |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Public **and** internal DNS failing | DNS FAILURE |
| 2 | rproxy-0 unreachable from the LAN but Cloudflare still reaches it | INTERNAL PATH FAILURE (LAN → rproxy-0) |
| 3 | rproxy-0 failing (TCP 443 closed) | FRONT PROXY FAILURE |
| 4 | rproxy-0 cannot reach rproxy-1 **and** rproxy-2 (measured on rproxy-0) | BACK PROXY LINK FAILURE |
| 5 | rproxy-1 **and** rproxy-2 down | BACK PROXY FAILURE |
| 6 | Backend host does not answer ping or the app port | BACKEND HOST UNREACHABLE |
| 7 | Host up, health endpoint failing | APPLICATION FAILURE |
| 8 | Only internal DNS failing / wrong answer | INTERNAL PATH FAILURE (DNS) |
| 9 | Only public DNS failing / private answer leaked | EXTERNAL PATH FAILURE (DNS) |
| 10 | Cloudflare returns 52x (origin unreachable) while rproxy-0 is fine from the LAN | EXTERNAL PATH FAILURE (Cloudflare → origin) |
| 11 | Cloudflare edge unreachable / TLS failure | EXTERNAL PATH FAILURE (edge) |
| 12 | rproxy-0 answers TCP but HTTPS/vhost/oauth2 check fails | FRONT PROXY DEGRADED |
| 13 | Anything partial or slow (one DNS server, standby proxy, slow hop) | DEGRADED |

**Probe limits.** On oauth2-protected sites, the Cloudflare and rproxy-0 probes stop at the oauth2-proxy sign-in page. They prove the edge, TLS, the vhost and oauth2-proxy, but not the backend. The backend is tested separately through rproxy-1 and rproxy-2 (same Host header). The Cloudflare probe starts inside the LAN and leaves through the home WAN, so a WAN outage shows up as an external path failure.
